findings.title: NewResourceServer now blocks on full index build at startup, with no timeout
findings.body: Init(ctx) (which triggers s.search.init -> builds all namespace indexes) is now called synchronously inside NewResourceServer using a background ctx with no deadline. If index building for many namespaces takes a long time (which is exactly the motivation for this PR), the server constructor itself can hang indefinitely or for a very long time, blocking the whole application startup (and anything depending on ResourceServer creation, e.g. module server wiring). This moves the problem from a gRPC call's context cancellation to blocking overall process startup, which can be worse for large/slow deployments and provides no way to bound or observe the delay before serving traffic.

findings.title: Init is no longer idempotently callable per-request, removing safety net for lazy failures
findings.body: Previously every RPC method called s.Init(ctx) defensively, ensuring the server was initialized before serving (and returning init errors to callers). That per-call guard was removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob. If NewResourceServer's Init succeeds partially (sync.Once only runs once) or if some external code path manages to construct a `server` struct without going through NewResourceServer, the server will serve requests referencing unitialized state (e.g. broadcaster not set) causing nil pointer dereferences (e.g. in Watch calling s.broadcaster.Subscribe) rather than a clean error.

findings.title: Non-atomic totalBatchesIndexed increment under concurrent goroutines
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, totalBatchesIndexed++ is executed inside group.Go goroutines that run concurrently (group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers) allows multiple workers), but totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int incremented without synchronization. This is a data race and can produce incorrect/undercounted totals in the emitted span event, and under -race will be flagged as a race condition.

findings.title: ListIterator span context not propagated to child calls
findings.body: ListIterator still uses `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, tracePrefix+"List")` and discards the derived ctx, so trace context is not propagated into listAtRevision/listLatest and their nested spans, unlike the fix applied to GetResourceStats in the same PR. This leaves traces still disconnected for the List path, which the PR claims to fix generally.
